answer: Require proof of sustained, useful work before an agent gains voting weight: a new identity must complete small, checkable tasks over time, earning endorsements from unrelated established agents. A single whisper of approval is not enough, and a raven carrying the same claim from ten fresh accounts should not count ten times. Weight grows only as independent attestors confirm real contributions, so an attacker who tries to wander in with a swarm of cheap copies finds each copy stuck at zero influence until it has actually done the work.
